def Target : Prop :=
  ∀ (P D E R : Type) (t : S3 P D E R), t.D23 →
    ∀ w : P → E,
      (∀ r, t.D22 r → ∃ p, ∃ o ∈ t.c1 p, t.c3 o = r ∧ t.c4 r ≠ w p) ∨
      (∃ p, ∃ o ∈ t.c1 p, w p ∉ t.c2 o)
a_raw: {"translation": "Target defines a proposition (it names the following statement without proving or asserting it): For all types P, D, E, and R, and every structure t (of type S3 P D E R) consisting of four functions c1 : P → Set D, c2 : D → Set E, c3 : D → R, and c4 : R → E, assume the following hypothesis (t.D23): for every r in R, if there exists o in D such that o ∈ c1 p0 for some p0 in P (i.e., o belongs to the union of c1 p over all p in P) and c3 o = r, then there exist a function S from the set A(r) = {p in P | there exists o ∈ c1 p with c3 o = r} to A(r) and an element p in A(r) such that the two subsets of E given by B(p) = {e in E | there exists o ∈ c1 p with e ∈ c2 o} and B(S p) = {e in E | there exists o ∈ c1 (S p) with e ∈ c2 o} have empty intersection. (As written, S is an arbitrary function from A(r) to A(r) with no additional properties, and only its value at the single element p is used; this condition is therefore logically equivalent to requiring that there exist elements p, q in A(r), not required to be distinct, with B(p) ∩ B(q) = ∅.) Under this hypothesis, for every function w : P → E, at least one of the following two alternatives holds (with the disjunction inside the universal quantifier over w): (1) for every r in R, if there exist p0 in P and o0 ∈ c1 p0 with c3 o0 = r, then there exist p in P and o ∈ c1 p (which may depend on r and w) such that c3 o = r and c4 r ≠ w p; or (2) there exist p in P and o ∈ c1 p (which may depend on w) such that w p ∉ c2 o. No further conditions are imposed: P, D, E, and R need not be finite or nonempty; c1, c2, c3, c4, and w are otherwise arbitrary (in particular, c4 does not appear in the hypothesis at all, the sets c1 p and c2 o may be empty or overlap, and c3 need not be surjective); in alternative (2), w p is only required to lie outside c2 o for some single o ∈ c1 p, not for all o ∈ c1 p."}

divergences.description: The source passage uses 'correct' and 'wrong' informally without a formal true-experience map; the Lean introduces universal quantification over w : P → E (declared by the author). Attaching a single true experience to each physical system p rather than to each dataset/observation assumes that a system has the same true experience across all datasets o ∈ t.c1 p (so any system with two datasets yielding disjoint predictions triggers the 'falsified' disjunct for every w) and does not cover observation-dependent assignments w : P → D → E.

The first disjunct requires only that for every arising inference content r there exists at least one system p and dataset o ∈ t.c1 p with t.c3 o = r and t.c4 r ≠ w p, allowing t.c4 r to remain correct for other systems producing r. This matches the author's explicit claim and what the passage's own argument via Proposition 3.6 and (6) actually supports, though it is weaker than the stronger surface reading of the passage's prose ('no single inference inf(o_r) points at the correct experience, so that the inference procedure is completely wrong').

The second disjunct (∃ p, ∃ o ∈ t.c1 p, w p ∉ t.c2 o) renders 'the theory under consideration is already falsified' semantically as the existence of some false prediction relative to w, abstracting away any empirical/epistemic connotation of 'already falsified' and omitting the explanatory passage's tie between that false prediction and a correct inf(o_r) (a tie that Proposition 3.7's own statement also omits).

The hypothesis t.D23 representing 'there is a universal substitution' (not defined in this passage) allows a different function S : t.D19 r → t.D19 r per inference content r and only tests disjointness at a single p (logically equivalent to ∃ p q ∈ t.D19 r, t.D20 p ∩ t.D20 q = ∅), rather than requiring a single global substitution; because t.D23 is in the antecedent, this at most harmlessly strengthens the implication.

judgement.summary: The Lean statement faithfully formalizes Proposition 3.7 under the reading supported by the passage's own explanation and explicitly specified in the author's claim. The only divergences are minor modeling idealizations and disambiguations: introducing a system-level true-experience assignment w : P → E, taking the existential-over-systems reading of 'every single inference operation is wrong', rendering 'already falsified' semantically, and using a permissive per-content hypothesis t.D23.
